text:
The burst pipe under the kitchen sink at our townhouse in Nonthaburi was found on the morning of 3 September, and the plumber, Wichai Saetang, thinks it had been leaking for about two days. The floor boards in the kitchen and hallway are swollen, and the lower cabinets have started to grow black mould along the back panels. My husband Kittipong says the insurer's policy covers sudden bursts but not gradual seepage, so how we describe the timing matters.

Since the mould started, my daughter's asthma has been worse. Her paediatrician, Dr Nattaya Prasert, wrote that she should not sleep in the downstairs room until the mould is professionally removed, and we are staying with my mother in the meantime. She has used her reliever inhaler twice a night since Monday.

The loss adjuster, Anucha Thongdee, is coming on Thursday at 2 pm. He asked for photos, the plumber's invoice for 4,800 baht, and the date we first noticed the damp. Please reach me on 081-555-0142 if he needs to change the visit.
task: Draft a letter to our insurer asking them to approve temporary accommodation for the family until the downstairs room can be used again.

text:
Before the contractor comes back I want to be clear about what I can actually pay. The insurance payout for the flooded bathroom is only 38 million rupiah, and it will be paid in one transfer, not in stages. My brother Agus Wijayakusuma has offered to lend me 10 million, but only if I repay it by March. I can find 15 million rupiah in cash this month without touching my emergency savings.

Pak Hendra Gunawan, the contractor, quoted 52 million rupiah for new waterproofing, tiles and a replacement vanity. He wants 50 percent on the day work starts, 30 percent when the tiling is finished and 20 percent after I sign off the final inspection. He says the vanity will take three weeks to arrive from the supplier, Bu Yulianti Nasution in Bekasi. His written quote does not mention any warranty, and I have not asked about one yet.

text:
The washing machine hose at our flat in Chiang Mai split while we were out, and the water came through the ceiling of the neighbour below, Khun Suda Kaewmanee. Her insurer has already contacted ours. The repair crew's foreman, Prasit Limsakul, says the wet plasterboard in our utility room has to be cut out, dried for at least five days and only then replaced. He cannot start before 12 November because the dehumidifier hire is booked until then.

Our own policy lists the cause as accidental damage, so I expect the excess of 5,000 baht to apply and I do not think the contents claim is worth making. The photos are all in the shared album, and the plumber's receipt is attached to the claim form I already sent.

I work rotating night shifts at the hospital laundry, and my supervisor, Ratchanee Boonmee, has only approved leave on 14 and 15 November. Outside those days I sleep until about 3 pm, so nobody will be home to open the door before then.

text: The storm on 20 October lifted several roof tiles on our house and rainwater ran down the wall of the main bedroom for about six hours before Somchai Wattanakul, our neighbour, noticed it and called me. We are behind on the mortgage by three instalments and the bank has agreed to wait until January, so we cannot pay the 8,000 baht excess up front. The roofer, Araya Panyawong, covered the opening with a tarpaulin on Sunday and says the permanent repair needs dry weather. text: Notes from the fire service's leaflet on drying a house after a minor flood. Turn off the electricity at the main switch before entering a wet room. Open windows for at least six hours a day and run a dehumidifier if the humidity stays above 60 percent. Lift rugs and move furniture away from walls so air can circulate. Do not use a heater with an open flame in a closed room. Wipe visible mould with detergent and water, wearing gloves and a mask, and throw away porous items such as mattresses that stayed wet for more than two days. Take dated photographs before cleaning in case you make an insurance claim.
